Button handles deep linking through a combination of Button Links, mobile SDKs, and attribution tokens:

Routes users to the best destination. A publisher passes Button the retailer’s destination URL. Button’s “Purchase Path” then opens the relevant page in the retailer’s installed app, sends the user through an app-install flow, or falls back to a mobile-web checkout.

Supports standard mobile-linking technologies. Brands configure a dedicated bttn.io domain that supports iOS Universal Links and Android App Links, with a fallback website for users who cannot open the app.

Button Developers
+1

Provides deferred deep linking after installation. When a user does not yet have the retailer’s app, Button can direct them to the app store. On the app’s first launch, the Merchant Library attempts to recover the original destination and attribution token, allowing the user to land on the intended product or page rather than the app homepage. 
Button Developers

In practical terms, Button’s value is that it combines destination routing and conversion attribution: the shopper gets the most appropriate app or web experience, while the publisher retains credit for the resulting transaction.

Button is more specialized than most ecommerce optimization platforms. It focuses on improving the post-click commerce journey, especially traffic from affiliates, creators, publishers, paid social, and mobile links. Its strengths include intelligent routing, deep linking into apps, app-install journeys, and conversion optimization after someone taps a link.

+1

impact.com

	Optimizing the journey before and during the handoff to the retailer’s web or app experience, particularly for offsite traffic.
VWO	Running deliberate A/B, multivariate, feature, and user-experience experiments across websites, apps, and backend systems.

	More automated, narrower optimization of mobile commerce links and destinations, without requiring teams to design every individual experiment.
When Button is the better choice

Button is most differentiated when:

A meaningful share of your sales comes from affiliate, creator, publisher, or paid-social traffic.

Mobile users frequently land on the mobile website even though the app converts better.

You already have an affiliate network but want to improve conversion per click, attribution visibility, or app adoption.

You want an optimization layer that can work alongside existing retailer and affiliate relationships.

Choose another category first when your primary problem is:

Partner recruitment and payouts: impact.com or another affiliate-management platform.

Company-wide mobile attribution: Branch or an equivalent mobile measurement platform.

Weak onsite search or recommendations: Nosto or another commerce-experience platform.

Website UX and checkout experimentation: VWO, Optimizely, or a dedicated CRO platform.

For a mature ecommerce company, the likely architecture is not Button versus everything else. It is:

Affiliate platform → Button optimization layer → retailer web/app experience → onsite personalization and experimentation.

Before adopting it, run a controlled test measuring incremental revenue per click, app-open rate, conversion rate, new-versus-existing customers, and margin after Button’s fees.
